reason: Moses is unambiguously portrayed as a national leader in this passage. The Israelites consistently appeal to him as their authority figure—they cry out to the Lord then speak directly to Moses with their grievances (expressing fear about dying in the wilderness and questioning why he led them out of Egypt). Moses responds authoritatively to calm the people (אַל־ תִּירָאוּ֒ - 'Do not fear'), directing their faith toward God's deliverance. Crucially, Moses performs the salvation miracle by stretching his hand over the sea, and the people's faith in him is explicitly stated at the end (וַיַּֽאֲמִ֙ינוּ֙ בַּֽיהוָ֔ה וּבְמֹשֶׁ֖ה עַבְדּֽוֹ - 'they believed in the Lord and in Moses His servant'). All these elements establish Moses as the established leader of the Israelite nation, not merely an aspiring one.
